Move is stated generally: applicability names two reusable patterns (single-index goal whose proof needs the property at every index -> universal strengthening; mutually dependent claims bundled into one conjunction for a single simultaneous induction) and cross-references extract-have for the standalone-lemma case. When-not-to-use is honest and specific: it explicitly admits that in this example the reduction is NOT routine (error-term argument at lines 1033-1426, verified in the copied file), so the suffices only buys a clean split, plus a false strengthening is a dead end. Consequences are honest and specific: new package obligation + reduction obligation, all-indices quantification risk, coupled conjuncts, silent-dead-end failure mode. Minor caveat, not enough to object: the coupling is one-directional in the proof (the A-claim step uses ih_b at line 1517, but the b-claim step does not use ih_A), so 'each induction step uses both halves' overstates slightly; the general lesson (bundle coupled claims to share hypotheses in one induction) still holds.
